meta.artifactName: State Parsing and Mapping Rules Document
meta.purpose: Rules for mapping diverse natural language expressions from source texts to canonical core composite states defined in Artifact 1 (Core Composite States Inventory Document). These rules support consistent extraction of enterState and exitState.

exampleQuotations: Don't be heedless. Don't later fall into regret.

A monk intent on heightened mind were to attend solely to the theme of concentration, it's possible that his mind would tend to laziness... it's possible that his mind would not be rightly concentrated for the ending of the effluents. But when he attends periodically to the theme of concentration, attends periodically to the theme of uplifted energy, attends periodically to the theme of equanimity, his mind is pliant, malleable, luminous, & not brittle. It is rightly concentrated for the ending of the effluents.
Don't give way to heedlessness or to intimacy with sensual delight–for a heedful person, the End-Maker holds him under his sway.
No recitation: the ruinous impurity. No heedfulness: the ruinous impurity.
Because of that gain, he becomes intoxicated, complacent, & falls into heedlessness.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies a state of contentment that can lead to heedlessness.

exampleQuotations: Ignorance has been destroyed; knowledge has arisen; darkness has been destroyed; light has arisen–as happens in one who remains heedful, ardent, & resolute.
Through initiative, heedfulness, restraint, & self-control, the wise would make an island no flood can submerge.
They have done their task with heedfulness. They are incapable of being heedless.
stateMappingRules.notes: Specifically for Arahants; implies a perfected state of heedfulness where regression is impossible.

exampleQuotations: A monk attending inappropriately brings unarisen effluents into play.
The instructed disciple of the noble ones, (however,) attends carefully & appropriately right there at the dependent co-arising.
Greed is a cause for the origination of actions.
Any desire-passion with regard to the earth property is a defilement of the mind.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the root of unskillful action.

exampleQuotations: Aversion is a cause for the origination of actions.
A monk in training… will make complete any training with regard to non-ill will.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the root of unskillful action; includes 'ill will' as a common manifestation.

exampleQuotations: Delusion is a cause for the origination of actions.
Defiled by ignorance, discernment does not develop.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the root of unskillful action; includes 'ignorance' as a common manifestation.

exampleQuotations: Non-greed is a cause for the origination of actions.
Non-aversion is a cause for the origination of actions.
Resolve for freedom from ill will.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the skillful root; includes 'non-ill will'.

exampleQuotations: Non-delusion is a cause for the origination of actions.
The five hindrances overwhelm awareness and weaken discernment.
A monk… secludes himself from sensuality, secludes himself from unskillful mental qualities, and enters & remains in the first jhāna… (where) the hindrances have been abandoned.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies when hindrances are no longer active.

exampleQuotations: The fetter of becoming, and who are released through right gnosis.
With the total ending of (the first) three fetters.
For me the ending of stress is reached; the ending of effluents, attained... The fetters are ended.
My mind is not released from the effluents through lack of clinging or sustenance.
If he wants, then through the ending of the effluents, he enters & remains in the effluent-free awareness-release & discernment-release.
The ending of effluents, attained.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the complete eradication of effluents.

exampleQuotations: If one doesn't stay obsessed with form... that's what one is measured by.

stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies abandonment of obsessions (no direct quotes found for 'obsessions abandoned' but implied by abandoning related defilements).

exampleQuotations: One is unvirtuous and hasn't abandoned the impurity of being unvirtuous. One is envious and hasn't abandoned the impurity of envy. One is stingy and hasn't abandoned the impurity of stinginess.
With impurities all blown away, unblemished, you'll reach the divine realm of the noble ones.
in whatever monk or nun there arises desire, passion, aversion, delusion, or mental resistance with regard to forms cognizable via the eye, he or she should hold the mind in check.
stateMappingRules.notes: Captures the presence of mental resistance towards sense objects or ideas.

exampleQuotations: He is mindful, endowed with excellent proficiency in mindfulness, remembering & able to call to mind even things that were done & said long ago.
The seven factors for awakening [mindfulness, analysis of qualities, persistence, rapture, calm, concentration, equanimity].
He keeps his persistence aroused for abandoning unskillful qualities and for taking on skillful qualities.
With persistence aroused for the highest goal's attainment.
In one whose heart is enraptured, the body grows calm.
His body calm, he feels pleasure.
His mind is concentrated & gathered into singleness.
equanimity-&-mindfulness purified
attaining pure equanimity, tranquility
I don't envision a single thing that, when undeveloped, is as unpliant as the mind. The mind, when undeveloped, is unconcentrated.

stateMappingRules.pattern: (?:^|\b)concentration that has a share in decline|wrong concentration\b
exampleQuotations: Concentration that has a share in decline is wrong concentration which focuses on sensuality, ill will & harmfulness.
When one has attained the first jhāna, the perception of sensuality has ceased.
When one has attained the second jhāna, directed thoughts & evaluations [verbal fabrications] have ceased.
When one has attained the third jhāna, rapture has ceased.
When one has attained the fourth jhāna, in-and-out breaths [bodily fabrications] have ceased.

stateMappingRules.pattern: (?:^|\b)concentration that has a share in distinction|noble distinction of knowledge & vision\b
exampleQuotations: Having transcended & calmed that abiding, lord, this is another comfortable abiding where a superior human attainment, a truly noble distinction of knowledge & vision, has been attained.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies states of concentration leading to distinction.

stateMappingRules.pattern: (?:^|\b)concentration that has a share in penetration|profound insight(?: leading to unbinding)?\b
exampleQuotations: The six perceptions conducive to penetration.
A monk endowed with these six qualities is capable of realizing the unexcelled cooled state.
There are these three feelings, my friend—feelings of pleasure, feelings of pain, and feelings of neither pleasure nor pain.
There are these three feelings, my friend—feelings of pleasure, feelings of pain, and feelings of neither pleasure nor pain.
There are these three feelings, my friend—feelings of pleasure, feelings of pain, and feelings of neither pleasure nor pain.
When one has attained the cessation of perception & feeling, perceptions & feelings [mental fabrications] have ceased.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the cessation of all feeling, a very high meditative attainment.

exampleQuotations: When one has attained the first jhāna, the perception of sensuality has ceased.
stateMappingRules.notes: Cessation of perception specific to sensuality.

exampleQuotations: When one has attained the dimension of the infinitude of space, the perception of forms has ceased.
stateMappingRules.notes: Cessation of perception specific to forms.

stateMappingRules.pattern: (?:^|\b)perception of the dimension of the infinitude of space has ceased\b
exampleQuotations: When one has attained the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness, the perception of the dimension of the infinitude of space has ceased.
stateMappingRules.notes: Cessation of perception specific to space.

stateMappingRules.pattern: (?:^|\b)perception of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness has ceased\b
exampleQuotations: When one has attained the dimension of nothingness, the perception of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness has ceased.
stateMappingRules.notes: Cessation of perception specific to consciousness.

stateMappingRules.pattern: (?:^|\b)perception of the dimension of nothingness has ceased\b
exampleQuotations: When one has attained the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, the perception of the dimension of nothingness has ceased.
stateMappingRules.notes: Cessation of perception specific to nothingness.

exampleQuotations: The perception of inconstancy, when developed & pursued, is of great fruit, of great benefit.
The perception of stress in what is inconstant, when developed & pursued, is of great fruit, of great benefit.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifying the perception of suffering within impermanence.

exampleQuotations: The perception of not-self in what is stressful, when developed & pursued, is of great fruit, of great benefit.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifying the perception of non-self within suffering.

exampleQuotations: When there is a delineation of thinking, it is possible that one will delineate a delineation of being assailed by the perceptions & categories of objectification.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the mind's active engagement in conceptual fabrication.

exampleQuotations: Resolve for sensuality… This is the right resolve with effluents, siding with merit, resulting in acquisitions.
Resolve for ill will… This is the right resolve with effluents, siding with merit, resulting in acquisitions.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies unskillful resolve for ill will.

exampleQuotations: Resolve for harmfulness… This is the right resolve with effluents, siding with merit, resulting in acquisitions.
Resolve for renunciation… This is the right resolve that is noble, without effluents, transcendent, a factor of the path.
Resolve for freedom from ill will… This is the right resolve that is noble, without effluents, transcendent, a factor of the path.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies skillful resolve for non-ill will.

exampleQuotations: Resolve for harmlessness… This is the right resolve that is noble, without effluents, transcendent, a factor of the path.
Defiled by ignorance, discernment does not develop.
The uninstructed run-of-the-mill person doesn't discern that as it has come to be… for the uninstructed run-of-the-mill person—there is no development of the mind.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies a lack or weakness in discernment.

exampleQuotations: This is called purity of view. (The thought,) 'I will make complete this sort of purity of view when it is not yet complete, or I will protect it here & there with discernment when it is complete': Any desire, effort, diligence, endeavor, relentlessness, mindfulness, & alertness there is called the factor for exertion with regard to purity of view.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the process of cultivating discernment.

exampleQuotations: He is discerning, endowed with the discernment of arising & passing away—noble, penetrating, leading to the right ending of stress.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies a well-developed faculty of discernment.

exampleQuotations: gnosis right here & now, or—if there be any remnant of clinging-sustenance—non-return.
And there many of my disciples remain, having attained the perfection & culmination of direct knowledge.
Clear knowing is the leader in the attainment of skillful qualities, followed by shame & compunction.
A person endowed with three things is to be recognized as a fool. Which three? Bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct.
Our bodily conduct will be pure, clear & open, unbroken & restrained.
Our verbal conduct… will be pure, clear & open, unbroken & restrained.
Our mental conduct will be pure, clear & open, unbroken & restrained.
He has right view and is not warped in the way he sees things.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies skillful mental conduct, including right view as its purest form.

exampleQuotations: They discern a released mind as 'a released mind,' and an unreleased mind as 'an unreleased mind.'
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies a mind still bound by defilements.

exampleQuotations: If he wants, then through the ending of the effluents, he enters & remains in the effluent-free awareness-release & discernment-release.
If he wants, then through the ending of the effluents, he enters & remains in the effluent-free awareness-release & discernment-release.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies liberation through insight and wisdom.

exampleQuotations: the realization of unbinding—in other words, the four establishings of mindfulness.
How very easeful: unbinding, as taught by the Rightly Self-awakened One—sorrowless, dustless, secure.
For me the ending of stress is reached; the ending of effluents, attained.
A monk endowed with six qualities is capable of realizing the unexcelled cooled state.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies a state of peace, free from the fires of defilement.

exampleQuotations: When the three forms of craving [for sensuality, for becoming, and for non-becoming] are comprehended.
When the three forms of craving [for sensuality, for becoming, and for non-becoming] are comprehended.
When the three forms of craving [for sensuality, for becoming, and for non-becoming] are comprehended.
Craving is the seamstress—for craving stitches one to the production of this or that very becoming.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the general presence of craving.

exampleQuotations: an uninstructed run-of-the-mill person regards form as: 'This is mine, this is my self, this is what I am.' He regards feeling… perception… fabrications… consciousness as: 'This is mine, this is my self, this is what I am.'
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies clinging to the five aggregates.

stateMappingRules.pattern: (?:^|\b)lack of clinging|no clinging|unagitated by lack of clinging\b
exampleQuotations: This, friends, is how non-agitation is caused by lack of clinging or sustenance.
associating with admirable friends
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies the external state of having supportive companions.

exampleQuotations: Over there are the roots of trees; over there, empty dwellings. Practice jhāna, monk.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies external environments conducive to practice.

exampleQuotations: Monks, gains, offerings, & fame are a cruel thing, a harsh, bitter obstacle to the attainment of the unexcelled rest from bondage.
stateMappingRules.notes: Identifies external factors that can be an obstacle.
